explanations: Wool is an animal fibre of protein, mostly from sheep, chemically closer to silk than to any plant fibre.
Cotton is a soft staple fibre of almost pure cellulose that grows in a boll around the seeds of the Gossypium shrub.
Linen is made from the bast fibres of flax: strong, absorbent, quick to dry and quick to crease.
Wool, cotton and linen are all natural fibres, taken from the bodies of plants or animals rather than made in a factory.

sources.excerpt: Wool is the textile fiber obtained from sheep and other mammals, especially goats, rabbits, and camelids.
Wool is an animal fiber and consists of protein together with a small percentage of lipids.
This makes it chemically quite distinct from cotton and other plant fibers, which are mainly cellulose, and akin to silk, another animal fiber composed primarily of protein.
Cotton is a soft, fluffy staple fiber that grows in a boll, or protective case, around the seeds of the cotton plants of the genus Gossypium in the mallow family Malvaceae.
The fiber is almost pure cellulose and may contain minor percentages of waxes, fats, pectins, and water.

Although cultivated since antiquity, it was the invention of the cotton gin that lowered the cost of production and led to its widespread use, and it is the most widely used natural fiber cloth in clothing today.
Linen () is a textile made from the bast fibers of the flax plant.
Linen is very strong and absorbent and dries faster than cotton.
Linen also has other distinctive characteristics, such as its tendency to wrinkle.
Natural fibers or natural fibres (see spelling differences) are fibers that are produced by geological processes or obtained from the bodies of plants or animals.
